key_insight: PerovAgent autonomously designs ligands for halide perovskite nanocrystals while turning its search observations into testable chemical design principles.
engineering_relevance: The framework could guide surface-ligand engineering for perovskite materials, but the abstract does not demonstrate solar-cell performance gains.
method: Use LLM-driven agents to propose ligands and construct atomistic surface models.
Evaluate binding energies with machine-learned interatomic potentials and iteratively refine candidates.
Statistically test inferred design principles and examine a recurring preference with density functional theory.
evidence_signal: Across 10 independent CsPbBr3 campaigns, 19 of 35 principles received prospective support, seven also passed a confound audit, and DFT reproduced the predicted alkynyl-phosphonate energetic preference.
watch_item: Binding-energy optimization alone does not establish ligand stability, experimental feasibility, or device-level benefits.
paper_title: PerovAgent: Autonomous Ligand Design for Halide Perovskite Nanocrystals
